findings.description: The no-resize test was strengthened (round-1 suggestion 1) and is now a real guard via the two-checkbox count — but the second new assertion `querySelectorAll('[data-test="step-keyboard-rows"] input[type="checkbox"]').toHaveLength(0)` is tautological. The persistent/onetime checkboxes live in a sibling `<div>` AFTER the `step-keyboard-rows` container closes (FunnelStepForm.vue: rows div 1603-1697, checkbox div 1699-1718), so there are never any checkboxes inside `step-keyboard-rows`. A future dev adding a resize_keyboard toggle would place it next to persistent/onetime in the keyboard-level checkbox div — exactly where a keyboard-wide toggle belongs — not inside the per-row editor. That addition would NOT be caught by this scoped-to-rows assertion. The other two assertions on this test (resize selector absent + exactly two named checkboxes resolve) carry the guard; this one adds no coverage.
findings.recommendation: Replace the rows-scoped check with the broader assertion round-1 actually recommended: `expect(document.querySelectorAll('[data-test^="step-keyboard"] input[type="checkbox"]')).toHaveLength(2)`. That counts ALL checkboxes in the SET_KEYBOARD subtree (persistent + onetime today) and trips the moment any third checkbox is rendered with a `step-keyboard-*` data-test, regardless of name — which is where a resize toggle would land. Keep the existing two named-checkbox `.filter(Boolean).length === 2` line as belt-and-suspenders. Non-blocking; the test already fails on the named-checkbox guard if either toggle disappears, so the regression surface is mostly covered — this only tightens the third-checkbox case.

summary: All three round-1 minor suggestions are resolved and verified against the component template. (1) The 'no resize_keyboard control' test (line 205) now asserts exactly two keyboard checkboxes via a filter(Boolean).length===2 guard plus a zero-checkboxes-in-rows-container check. (2) A new 'blocks submit on blank CLEAR_KEYBOARD text' case (line 217) exercises the previously-untested CLEAR-branch text gate — mounts, selects CLEAR_KEYBOARD, sets whitespace text, asserts the rendered text error AND no submit emit. (3) The SET render test (line 92) now pins the seed to EXACTLY one row with one button via toHaveLength(1) on step-keyboard-row-* plus negative assertions on button-0-1/button-1-0, making the cap/add-remove tests' 1→N arithmetic load-bearing. Spec now has 19 cases. Every data-test selector used maps to a real attribute in the SET_KEYBOARD/CLEAR_KEYBOARD template (verified: step-keyboard-text/-error, -button-error-r-c, -hint-r-c, -duplicate-error, -persistent, -onetime, -add-row, -add-button-r, -remove-row-r, -remove-button-r-c) — no hallucinated selectors. Litmus tests pass throughout: validation cases assert both rendered error and absent emit; emit cases assert concrete step shape (id/next preserved, keyboardRows deep-equal, trimmed texts, CLEAR omits keyboard-only fields, explicit false/true checkbox seed catching the ?? default-clobber bug); the inactive/non-keyword hint case (line 248) discriminates active+keyword from paused/on_start funnels; the hint-never-blocks case (line 259) confirms the advisory contract. Isolation is sound: beforeEach resets the real-Pinia store to [], afterEach clears document.body, and store-seeding deliberately runs AFTER the type switch fires ensureFunnelsLoaded's overwriting fetch (clearly commented). One residual minor: a single tautological rows-scoped checkbox assertion that does not guard the regression it targets (the real guard is the named-checkbox count beside it). Status: passed; one optional hardening tweak, no blocking or major issues.
